transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nora Li (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Borealis Head of ML Ops), Liam Ortega (Security), Priya Singh (Product), Diego Ramos (SRE)

Auto-generated summary: Align on onboarding runbook and networking, capture compliance needs, define pilot KPIs.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll give about 45 minutes and save 5 for next steps, uh i'm alex from redwood inference, with samir our se and nora cs. who wants to kick off on the borealis side?
[00:12] Maya (Maya Chen): yeah thanks alex, appreciate it. we wanted to walk through the runbook, make sure we map out the network steps — we have fairly strict regs for PHI handling so encryption at rest and audit logs are big for us. also timeline: we'd like a pilot in prod-like env by end of may.
[00:28] Alex: great, that's helpful. pilot by end of may gives us about seven weeks. samir, can you do a quick overview of typical runbook items we send?
[00:36] Samir (SE): sure. so our onboarding runbook is broken into: infra prep (vpc peering or privatelink, route tables), credentials & auth (sso/saml, api keys, k m s), data flow and retention (what's logged, kv cache retention), perf bench plan (latency targets, token throughput), and rollback/playback steps. we usually recommend dedicated for PHI customers but hosted with VPC private link is also possible depending on commit and isolation needs.
[01:05] Priya (Product): quick clarifying q: when you say dedicated, you mean redwood dedicated reserved gpu pools? what's the minimum commit?
[01:12] Alex: yes dedicated is reserved capacity where you get predictable throughput and an SLA; pricing/commit varies but we'll send rough tiers. for onboarding pilot most folks start on hosted+private link or a small dedicated pool for consistent perf.
[01:26] Liam (Security): on encryption — we need to confirm customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). is that available for private deployments only or also for hosted with VPC?
[01:34] Samir: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS. for hosted with PrivateLink there are options to encrypt and we provide segregated key options but full HSM/PKI may require private. i'll follow up with exact matrix in the doc.
[01:52] Diego (SRE): network-wise we're leaning away from peering because of cross-account routing complexity. private link would be cleaner for our infra team, any caveats?
[01:59] Samir: PrivateLink is generally simpler for inbound egress constraints; it depends on whether you need SNAT or persistent peering for internal services. latency is typically slightly better with peering but difference is small, and privatelink reduces blast radius. we'll include a decision matrix.
[02:18] Maya: also curious about logs retention; clinical audit requires 7 years for some artifacts, is that something redwood can support on request?
[02:26] Nora (CSM): we have configurable retention windows and for enterprise customers extended retention is available as an add-on. note that storing logs longer may incur cost and we can tie it to your retention policy in the runbook.
[02:42] Maya: ok thanks. on the pilot KPIs — core ones are: 95th pct latency under 250ms for 512-token prompts, throughput of 50 reqs/s for steady-state, and model hallucination rate under our threshold on the prompt suite.
[02:58] Samir: that is good, we'll aim to replicate those in the pre-prod load test. we recommend a mix of synthetic and real prompt replay to exercise kv cache and prefix caching.
[03:12] Priya: do you have guidance on quantization/accuracy tradeoffs? we want to control cost but can't degrade quality past a point.
[03:19] Samir: yes — we can run a couple model variants: full precision for exposures where accuracy matters and quantized 4-bit variants for bulk tasks; our optimize team can help pick layers to quantize that minimally impact your eval metrics. we'll include recommended profiles.
[03:36] Liam: on the compliance front — SOC 2 is ok, but we also need iso and localized data residency notes for eu; do you have regional hosting?
[03:46] Alex: we host in multiple regions; for EU residency we can place the workspace in eu-west regions and provide audit logs. we'll attach the SOC2, ISO 27001 excerpts and data-residency notes.
[03:58] Maya: one thing — we may require service accounts and least privilege integration with our vault. can you integrate with HashiVault or azure keyvault?
[04:08] Samir: we already have integrations with several KMS providers; for vaults we can support a service account style and rotate keys via your vault solution — i'll check the exact flow and include a sample policy.
[04:24] Alex: let's talk about runbook cadence — we usually split onboarding into three sprints: sprint zero (network, auth, security docs), sprint one (pilot config, smoke tests), sprint two (load test and go/no-go). each sprint is 1-2 weeks depending on customer bandwidth.
[04:41] Maya: sounds good. sprint zero is the priority, we want network and an initial smoke test by 2026-04-28.
[04:48] Nora: noted — we'll set up a joint task list. i've put a few owners in the action items.
[04:55] Diego: practical question — do you expose token-level cost breakdowns during testing? our finance folks want visibility.
[05:03] Alex: yes the console exposes token-level costing, and we can produce per-session breakdowns. during pilot we can share hourly reports so you can track burn.
[05:12] Priya: procurement timeline — we may need a PO in place before starting dedicated; is there a way to start with hosted and then flip to dedicated without major rework?
[05:22] Samir: we design the deployment abstraction so you can transition; pins for model versions, config and rollouts are portable. we'll document the migration path and expected downtime (minimal).
[05:35] Maya: any blockers you foresee?
[05:38] Samir: the biggest typical blockers are: network allowlists and service-account permissions, encryption KMS policy approvals, and getting a representative prompt set for hallucination metrics. if we can get those early we avoid delays.
[05:53] Liam: we'll start the security questionnaire now and aim to complete it next week.
[05:58] Alex: perfect. next steps recap — we'll send runbook template & security docs, se will send load test plan, and customer provides network details and questionnaire.
[06:10] Maya: perfect thank you all.
[06:14] Alex: thanks everybody, we'll follow up with artifacts.

End of transcript.
